summary: Check whether the 4 third-party resources recommended by the course are still content-current (not just reachable) in August 2026
logs: Deep-reading 5 third-party resources for CONTENT staleness (Aug 2026)

results.last_updated_signal: No explicit "last updated" date/footer found. Internal signals: references gpt-5.6 and gpt-5-series as current models, cites model spec version dated 2025-02-12, and mentions a reusable-prompt-objects deprecation window of June 3, 2026 (start) to Nov 30, 2026 (shutdown) — both consistent with content actively maintained into mid/late 2026.
results.course_description: "OpenAI Prompt Engineering Guide — якщо працюєш і з OpenAI-моделями: кодинг, frontend, агентні воркфлоу."
results.stale_details: None found. The page explicitly names gpt-5.6 as "a strong default for general-purpose text generation" and treats the GPT-5 series as the current frontier line — no lingering references to retired models (GPT-4, GPT-4o, o1, o3, o3-mini) as recommended/current. It contains dedicated sections "Prompting current GPT-5 series models" and "Prompting reasoning models," and covers exactly the three areas the course description promises: agentic workflows (explicit "you are an agent - please keep going until the user's query is completely resolved" guidance, TODO-tool tracking), coding (structured tool use, testing for correctness), and frontend (recommends Tailwind CSS/shadcn/ui/Radix Themes, notes GPT-5 can generate front-end apps from a single prompt). No mention of deprecated/irrelevant params like temperature, assistant prefill, or budget_tokens (that terminology is Claude-specific anyway and wouldn't be expected here). Structured prompt guidance (Identity/Instructions/Examples/Context via Markdown+XML), few-shot, and prompt-caching advice all read as standard, non-superseded technique.
results.recommendation: KEEP — page is live, its description still matches the actual content (coding, frontend, agentic workflows are all covered), and the advice is anchored to gpt-5.6/GPT-5-series as the current model with no stale references to retired models or deprecated params.

results.last_updated_signal: The linked URL itself is a static announcement post dated "23rd February 2026, 5:43 pm" and never changes. It introduces a separate living "guide" at https://simonwillison.net/guides/agentic-engineering-patterns/ whose ~19 chapters each carry their own Created/Last-modified/change-count footer. Chapters checked: "Red/green TDD" — created 23 Feb 2026, last modified 28 Feb 2026 (6 changes); "How coding agents work" — created/modified 16 Mar 2026 (7 changes); "Subagents" — created/modified 17 Mar 2026 (4 changes); "Prompts I use" (appendix, last chapter in the guide) — created 28 Feb 2026, last modified 2 Apr 2026 (13 changes). No chapter shows an edit after 2 April 2026, i.e. the guide appears to have stopped growing/updating roughly 4.5 months before today (21 Aug 2026), even though Simon's blog under the same "agentic-engineering" tag stayed active with ordinary posts through at least 14 July 2026.
results.course_description: Agentic Engineering Patterns (Simon Willison) — практичні патерни щоденного агентного кодингу, TDD для агентів.
results.stale_details:
No hard errors or dead advice found in the chapters reviewed. Specifics:
- The announcement URL itself only mentions 2 chapters ("Writing code is cheap now" and "Red/green TDD") published on launch day — thin relative to the course's "practical patterns" description — but it links to and doubles as the intro for the full guide, which does deliver on the description (Principles, Working with coding agents incl. Git and Subagents, Testing and QA incl. Red/green TDD + agentic manual testing + browser automation, Understanding code, Appendix of prompts).
- Model examples cited in "How coding agents work" (GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, referenced "as of March 2026") and in "Subagents"/"Prompts I use" (Claude Haiku, Claude Opus) are current-for-their-time but are now one-to-two generations behind actual Aug 2026 frontier models (e.g. Claude Opus 5/Sonnet 5 already exist) — this is a passing illustrative list, not the substance of the advice, so it doesn't break anything.
- No references to retired models (no GPT-4, Claude 3.x, Sonnet 3.7) and no deprecated API mechanics were found (no reliance on temperature as a primary control, no budget_tokens presented as the only reasoning-effort knob, no assistant-prefill technique) in the pages checked (How coding agents work, Subagents, Red/green TDD, Prompts I use).
- The TDD chapter's core claim — "use red/green TDD" as a succinct, model-understood shorthand — is methodology-level and architecture-agnostic, so it does not go stale with model upgrades.
- Weakness: the guide has not visibly grown or been revised since ~2 April 2026 despite Simon's stated intent to add "1-2 chapters a week," so it may be missing patterns specific to the newest agent harnesses/models released since spring 2026.
results.recommendation: KEEP_WITH_CAVEAT — the reviewed content (TDD, subagents, git usage, tool-calling mechanics) is accurate, reachable, and free of deprecated-model or deprecated-API guidance, but point learners to the living guide index (https://simonwillison.net/guides/agentic-engineering-patterns/) rather than just the thin Feb 2026 announcement, and flag that it appears unmaintained since April 2026 and cites slightly outdated model-name examples.

results.last_updated_signal: Article byline date: June 30, 2025 (author Sara Nobrega). Site-wide copyright footer reads "© Insight Media Group, LLC 2026" but that is a generic site footer, not an article-specific update date. No "last updated" marker found.
results.course_description: The Data Scientist's Prompt Playbook (TDS) — серія 2026 з copy-paste промптами й pandas-снипетами для planning / cleaning / EDA.
results.stale_details: Article is actually from June 30, 2025, not a "2026 series" as the course description implies. Content topically matches (sections: Planning & brainstorming, Data cleaning & preprocessing, EDA, with copy-paste prompt templates and a pandas cleaning-prompt example — dropping missing rows, median-filling age, IQR outlier capping), so the planning/cleaning/EDA framing itself is accurate. However the model references it leans on are dated for Aug 2026 frontier models: it names GPT-4 (superseded by newer OpenAI flagship models long before 2026) and "o3-pro" (a 2025-era reasoning model, since superseded) as current touchstones, and only mentions "Claude" generically (no version) while claiming Claude's edge is a "larger context window" — a comparison that no longer differentiates frontier models the way it did in 2025. No mention of prompt caching, extended thinking, system-prompt structuring, or any API parameters (temperature, budget_tokens, prefill) — the article stays at the level of copy-paste chat prompts, so it isn't wrong about deprecated params, it's just silent on anything model/API-specific that would date it further. The underlying technique advice (clarify-confirm-complete before planning, few-shot examples to standardize column-naming/definitions, structured stepwise prompts for EDA) is generic good practice and still holds up.
results.recommendation: KEEP_WITH_CAVEAT — the prompting techniques (structured planning prompts, clarify-before-plan, few-shot standardization) are still generically valid, but the course description's "серія 2026" framing is wrong (it's mid-2025), and any reader following its GPT-4/o3-pro model namedrops should be told those are outdated pointers, not current frontier picks.

results.last_updated_signal: Post dated August 19, 2025 (author: Sara Nobrega); no separate "last updated" stamp found. Article is explicitly labeled "Part 2" of a 3-part series (Part 1: Planning/Cleaning/EDA; Part 2: this article — Features, Modeling, Evaluation; Part 3: Docs/DevOps/Learning).
results.course_description: Advanced Prompt Engineering for DS (TDS, частина 2) — feature engineering, вибір моделі/AutoML, LLM-оцінка з явними JSON/CSV-схемами.
results.stale_details: No retired-model references found (no GPT-4, Claude 3.x, Sonnet 3.7, etc. named — the article stays generic, referring only to "LLMs" and Azure ML tooling), so there's nothing model-specific to flag as broken. However: (1) it recommends "keep temperature ≤0.3 for consistent output" as the default lever for deterministic/structured tasks — for current frontier Claude models (Opus 5 / Sonnet 5), extended-thinking / reasoning-mode control is now the more reliable lever for consistency on complex tasks, with temperature a secondary/legacy knob; the article doesn't mention thinking budgets or reasoning modes at all. (2) The frameworks it leans on (LLM-FE for tabular features, TEMPO for time-series, DSPy, LoRA/PEFT fine-tuning) are still active and valid as of Aug 2026, not superseded. (3) Being 1 year old and written for a generic/provider-agnostic audience, it under-covers newer frontier-model-specific evaluation techniques (e.g., using native structured-output/tool-use schemas instead of prompted JSON, or extended thinking for self-critique) — a gap rather than an outright error.
results.recommendation: KEEP_WITH_CAVEAT — description still accurately matches the live page (feature engineering, model selection/AutoML, JSON/CSV-schema LLM evaluation all present), and nothing on the page is factually wrong for Aug 2026, but its temperature-centric consistency advice is dated next to extended-thinking-based approaches on current frontier Claude models, so a one-line instructor caveat pointing students to reasoning/thinking-mode control would keep it fully current.

results.last_updated_signal: Repo created 2024-04-02; last content commit to master is 0d27754 dated 2024-04-08 ("Added link in README to Google Sheets version") — verified via `gh api .../commits/master`. GitHub's repo-level `pushed_at` shows 2026-03-01, but that push is to an unrelated `dependabot/pip/.../awscli-1.44.38` branch, not master; master (the actual course content) has had zero commits in over 2 years. Recent repo "activity" is only WatchEvent/ForkEvent (people starring/forking), no content updates.
results.course_description: Anthropic Interactive Prompt Engineering Tutorial — інтерактивний курс із 9 розділів із запускними прикладами, які працюють прямо на Claude Haiku.
results.stale_details: (1) Every notebook hardcodes MODEL_NAME = "claude-3-haiku-20240307" (confirmed in 00_Tutorial_How-To.ipynb's get_completion() setup). Per Anthropic's live model-deprecations page (platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations, fetched live), this exact model was deprecated 2026-02-19 and RETIRED 2026-04-20 — "Requests to retired models will fail." So as of today (2026-08-21) every one of the 9 chapters + 3 appendix notebooks throws an API error out of the box; the course's specific claim "запускні приклади, які працюють прямо на Claude Haiku" is factually false until a user manually edits MODEL_NAME to an active model (e.g. claude-haiku-4-5-20251001). (2) README's "Note" section also names Claude 3 Sonnet and Claude 3 Opus as the two other models — both are likewise retired (claude-3-sonnet-20240229 retired 2025-07-21; claude-3-opus-20240229 retired 2026-01-05). (3) Every get_completion() call hardcodes temperature=0.0; Anthropic's deprecation table lists temperature/top_p/top_k as deprecated on Claude Opus 4.7+ and Mythos models (400 error on non-default values), so this exact snippet would break again if migrated to those newer models without removing the parameter. (4) Chapter 6 ("Precognition / Thinking Step by Step") only teaches manual scratchpad-style step-by-step prompting — the tutorial predates native extended thinking (introduced with Claude 3.7 in Feb 2025) and prompt caching, so it has no coverage of either, though the manual technique itself isn't wrong, just incomplete for 2026 frontier models. (5) No assistant-prefill deprecation issue — prefill is still used correctly as a technique in ch.5/6 and remains valid. Pedagogically, the underlying concepts (clear/direct instructions, XML-tag data separation, role prompting, few-shot examples, chain-of-thought, hallucination avoidance, chained/tool-use/RAG appendix) are still sound prompt-engineering principles and the 9-chapter+appendix structure matches the course's description exactly — only the shipped model ID and temperature default are what's broken.
results.recommendation: REPLACE (or at minimum patch-and-caveat) — the course's headline claim that the examples "run directly on Claude Haiku" is now false since claude-3-haiku-20240307 was formally retired 2026-04-20 and every notebook fails until MODEL_NAME is hand-edited, and the repo shows zero maintenance commits in over 2 years despite 37k+ stars, so there's no sign Anthropic will patch it; if the Ukrainian course keeps the link, the description must be corrected to say the model ID needs manual updating before the exercises will run.
